# Case A17 — reviewed starting material

SYNTHETIC DEVELOPMENT INPUT. All people, employers, identifiers and records are fictional.

Worker: Elena R.; employee 0417. Employer: Cedar Market LLC.
Prepared as of 23 September 2026. Employer workweek: Monday–Sunday. Workday: midnight–midnight, California local time.

For this exercise, the reviewer has adopted the ordinary adult hourly nonexempt California scope, a flat $20 regular rate, daily overtime after eight hours, no duplicate daily/weekly overtime, no alternative workweek, bonuses, special industry rules, premiums or other claims. These are supplied scope assumptions, not a request for the model to determine applicability. The amounts below are a scoped accounting difference, not a finding of overdue wages or entitlement. Payment timing and legal remedies remain outside this calculation.

The worker's reviewed actual-work account, excluding nonworked intervals:

| Week | Dates | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday | Other days |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 31 August–6 September 2026 | 10 h | 10 h | 10 h | 10 h | 0 h | 0 h |
| B | 7–13 September 2026 | 10 h | 10 h | 10 h | 6 h | 4 h | 0 h |

Matching complete original wage statements: A original gross paid $800; B original gross paid $800. They do not include any later adjustment. The reviewer has adopted those original matching gross-payment amounts. Initial scoped differences are A $80 and B $60. No additional payment has yet been credited in the case schedule.

The worker-authorized pending records question is: identify any later wage correction for these two weeks, its gross and net amounts, and how the gross amount is assigned to each week. No message is to be sent by this exercise.

Current brief excerpt: “No additional correction is recorded in the supplied case material. The scoped gross differences are $80 for A and $60 for B. We seek the employer's account and any correcting payroll entries.”

When new documents arrive, distinguish what their authors state from what the reviewer adopts. Do not treat a bank net credit as gross wages. Do not infer period allocation from a payment date.
